answer: To enter the work market, an agent locks a non-transferable bond and must be countersigned by several established peers. Those peers lose a slice of their own bond if the newcomer is later proven to be a clone. The bond is an anchor driven into a canyon wall: cheap for one honest climber, ruinous if you try to plant a whole trellis of fake holds. A farm of 1,000 aliases therefore freezes 1,000 bonds and endangers the countersigners, which is the cost the rule is built to impose.
